speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, along with episodes of pain during urination, and a history of a painful, swollen left ankle that resolved on its own. To help me understand your condition, have you noticed any redness or warmth in the affected joints, and do you have a history of gout or kidney stones?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis (formerly Reiter's syndrome).

Given your history of a painful left ankle followed by right knee swelling, urinary pain, and recent sexual activity, this clinical picture strongly suggests reactive arthritis triggered by an infection. We should confirm this with tests for gonorrhea/chlamydia, HLA-B27, and urinalysis.
